subject: Pilot criteria, model stack and localization plan - Leximart
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Recap + proposed pilot criteria and model stack (next steps)

Hi Sofia / Leximart team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete set of next steps so we can kick off a focused 3-week pilot: 

High-level objective
- Validate retrieval + LLM answer quality for product QA workflows across EN/ES/FR and measure cost/latency tradeoffs.

Success criteria (must-haves for acceptance)
- Relevance/accuracy: >= 85% on the provided 150-sample QA rubric (precision on answer extraction + correctness).
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 350ms on a 4 GPU Redwood Dedicated equivalent profile.
- Throughput: support sustained 8 QPS with <10% tail-slowing under our suggested batching.
- Stability: no functional regressions versus control prompts over the evaluation set.

Proposed evaluation plan (week-by-week)
- Week 0 (pre-kick): exchange NDA + sample data bucket (read-only S3 or shared Drive).
- Week 1: data ingestion + embedding index build, baseline embedding recall metrics, initial reranker wiring.
- Week 2: run generation experiments across model candidates for EN/ES/FR, collect automated metrics + 50 human evals.
- Week 3: iterate on prompt templates, finalize acceptance testing and handoff checklist.

Model stack recommendation for pilot
- Primary (generation & chat): Llama-3-Chat-13B (FP16 quantized) — chosen for strong instruction-following and efficient scaling on our runtime.
- Fallback / lightweight option: Mistral-7B-Instruct (8-bit) — for cost-sensitive paths and lower-latency shallow answers.
- Retrieval & embeddings: Open-Embedding-3-small for dense retrieval; use re-ranking with a 2-stage approach (embedding recall -> reranker generation).

Multilingual approach
- We'll run bilingual prompts natively where possible; for Spanish/French we recommend: a) language-aware tokenization + cased prompt variants, and b) a small translation-check pipeline for corner cases. No mandatory fine-tune required for pilot; we'll measure whether a small adapter yields material gains during Week 2.

Ownership and roles
- Redwood lead: Michael Grant (pilot owner, commercial/coordination).
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao (technical owner, runtime/model ops).
- Redwood CSM: Marissa Cole (logistics, acceptance criteria).
- Leximart: Sofia Rios (product lead), Carlos Mendes (QA lead), devops@leximart.com (infra contact).

Immediate asks for kickoff
1) Please confirm the read-only S3 path or Drive folder with a 100–200 sample set (mixed EN/ES/FR) by EOD Friday.
2) Confirm that Leximart's devops can open port access for our temporary test runner or provide an IP allowlist.
3) Sign the attached one-page pilot charter (redwood-poc-charter-v1.pdf).

Attachments: redwood-poc-charter-v1.pdf, sample-data-schema.csv (see suggested data columns).

I'll pencil in a kickoff for Monday 2028-03-20 11:00am PT unless you propose otherwise.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed pilot criteria and model stack (next steps)

Thanks Michael — and thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Data & privacy: Our QA dataset includes customer-provided transcripts that must remain in-region (US). Do you support an in-region-only processing option for the pilot, or would that require Private deployment?

2) Token limits: what prompt + context length should we expect for the Llama-3-Chat-13B config you proposed? Some of our product pages are long (~8–10k chars).

3) Embeddings vs rerank: we want to confirm whether the approach will be embeddings-first (dense retrieval) + generator rerank (recommended) or generator-only retrieval for extraction tasks.

Also looping in Carlos (QA lead) — Carlos, can you confirm the sample schema and whether 150 examples for human eval is feasible on your side? We can expand if needed.

Finally — can Redwood provide a short bilingual demo (EN/ES) showing the same prompt answered in both languages so our stakeholders can see parity?

Best,
Sofia
Product Manager, Leximart
sofia@leximart.com

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed pilot criteria and model stack (next steps)

Hi Sofia — quick technical clarifications inline: 

- In-region processing: For the pilot we can run in a hosted region that is US-only (data residency at the region level). Private on-prem/VPC would be required for strict customer-managed hardware. I can surface region-specific S3 access options in the kickoff.

- Prompt/context length: Llama-3-Chat-13B on our runtime comfortably supports sequences up to 32k tokens in experimental configs; for the pilot we recommend a working context of 8k tokens to reduce memory pressure and ensure the latency SLO. For longer product pages we suggest chunking + per-chunk retrieval + a short fuse/re-rank prompt.

- Retrieval architecture: we strongly recommend embeddings-first dense retrieval followed by a generator reranker for extraction accuracy and cost control. That aligns with your acceptance criteria (precision + throughput). We'll provide sample notebook that wires Open-Embedding-3-small into FAISS/annoy and shows rerank steps.

- Bilingual demo: happy to provide — attaching a short ops note and example payloads (model-ops-play.pdf). We'll demo parity by running the same QA prompt translated to Spanish and French and comparing outputs.

Operational suggestions (pilot tuning)
- Start with 512-token generation cap for QA answers and increase only if evaluation shows truncation.
- Use request-level KV cache warmups for repeated session queries.
- Recommended batching: 8–16 concurrent requests per GPU for the 13B profile; smaller batch sizes for Mistral fallback.

Attaching: model-ops-play.pdf with config examples and quantization tradeoffs.

- Aditya
